entries.finding: 'Every living thing has a two-part scientific name'
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute. Names belong to species, and many species have none yet.
entries.change: Now 'Every species is given a two-part scientific name'.

entries.finding: Q2 and Q3 share the nymph diagram
entries.reason: Q2's hints never mention moulting or growth. Q3's hints never name the insect.

entries.finding: Hint 3 says moulting happens only to animals with a hard outer covering, and only while they grow
entries.reason: False absolute. Snakes shed their skin, and birds and mammals moult too.
entries.change: Hint 3 now says the other option is how a young insect gets round a hard covering that cannot stretch.

entries.finding: Solution calls locomotion a feature of all living things and says the insect moves at every life stage
entries.reason: Plants do not locomote and an insect egg does not move. Hint 2 said the same thing ('throughout the insect's whole life').
entries.change: How to tell now says the other three carry on into adult life and do not make the insect bigger. B line now says the adult moves too. Hint 2 now says respiration and locomotion carry on after the insect becomes an adult.

entries.finding: 'A simple dicot leaf has a pointed tip' stated for all dicot leaves
entries.reason: Many dicot leaves have rounded or notched tips.
entries.change: Scoped to 'A simple dicot leaf like the one drawn'.

entries.finding: Q4 and Q5 share the leaf diagram
entries.reason: Q4's hints never name label II or the midrib. Q5 hint 3 says two of the labels are the apex and axil but never says which letters they are.

entries.finding: Treats the midrib and veins as the same thing as vascular bundles
entries.reason: Over-reach. 'Veins are the vascular bundles that carry xylem and phloem' is how the syllabus puts it and is correct at that level. The supporting tissue around a vein is beyond the syllabus.

entries.finding: Exam tip: 'in any leaf, stem or root, xylem and phloem are always found together in vascular bundles'
entries.reason: False for roots, where xylem and phloem lie on separate radii. The syllabus teaches this.
entries.change: Now 'in leaves and stems, xylem and phloem run together in vascular bundles'.

entries.finding: 'the vacuole has nothing to do with it' is too absolute
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute (check 11). The standard gives this exact case: the vacuole plays a part in some plant movements.
entries.change: D line now says sensitivity is not one of the functions the syllabus gives to the vacuole.

entries.finding: Q8 shares the salt-solution stem with Q7
entries.reason: Q7 is settled as defective and gets no teaching. Nothing to leak into.

entries.finding: Q11 and Q12 share the phagocytosis diagram, forward direction
entries.reason: Q11's hints never mention white blood cells, blood or any body system.

entries.finding: Diagram has no alt text
entries.reason: Alt text is written separately in out/diagrams/biology-waec.alt.json and is not part of the teaching item. Checks 1 to 10 passed.

entries.finding: Hint 2 says bacteria are engulfed 'by phagocytes', which answers Q11 (phagocytosis) by word match
entries.reason: Check 12 does not say which direction a leak goes. The practice page has a question navigator, so a student can open Q12's hints before answering Q11. The fix is one phrase.
entries.change: Hint 2 now says the cells that engulf and destroy bacteria in this way are a type of white blood cell.

entries.finding: Hint 2 nearly gives away B, and hint 3 leaves B as the only choice
entries.reason: Hint 2 gives the deciding principle, which is its job. Hint 3 narrows to two and poses the test, which is as strong as the worked example's hint 3. The student still has to connect light to a root in dark soil, and remember the question asks for the wrong statement.

entries.finding: Most water is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule, not 'especially in the loop of Henle and the collecting duct'
entries.reason: Fact error (check 8).
entries.change: Principle now says most water is taken back into the blood as the filtrate flows along the tubule, and names no segment.

entries.finding: Urine is not always more concentrated than blood
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute (check 11). Someone who drinks a lot of water makes dilute urine.
entries.change: 'so urine becomes more concentrated than blood' now reads 'so urine usually ends up more concentrated than blood'.

entries.finding: The option C reasoning misleads, because adding a solute does raise concentration
entries.reason: The claim that adding one substance cannot concentrate the rest was weak, and hint 3 relied on it. C is wrong because urea gets in mainly by filtration.
entries.change: C line now says urea gets into the tubule mainly by filtration at the glomerulus, not by active secretion. Hint 3 now asks how urea gets into the tubule and what the kidney takes back from the filtrate in the largest amount.

entries.finding: 'sympathetic action reduces saliva' is too categorical
entries.reason: Over-reach. Less saliva under sympathetic action is what the syllabus teaches, and it is true of the watery flow. 'Reduces' is not an absolute.

entries.finding: Not every perennial fruits again and again
entries.reason: Unscoped claim about all perennials (check 11). Some flower once and then die.
entries.change: B line now says 'and most, like mango and orange trees, fruit again and again'.

entries.finding: Hint 3 implies every kind of food is chemically digested
entries.reason: Water, vitamins and mineral salts are absorbed without being digested.
entries.change: Hint 3 now asks which option describes chemical digestion correctly for proteins and fats as well as starch. The principle adds one sentence saying water, vitamins and mineral salts are absorbed without being digested.

entries.finding: Hint 1 and the solution say all digested food goes into the blood
entries.reason: Most digested fat goes into the lacteals and lymph. The syllabus teaches this.
entries.change: Hint 1 now says 'pass through the gut wall and be absorbed'. The principle now says 'into the blood or lymph'.

entries.finding: Exam tip: 'digestion always goes large to small and insoluble to soluble'
entries.reason: Sucrose, maltose and lactose dissolve in water but still have to be digested.
entries.change: Now 'digestion turns large molecules into small ones, and usually turns insoluble ones into soluble ones'.

entries.finding: Exam tip says 'blood that will not clot' and that lack of vitamin K 'stops blood from clotting'
entries.reason: Overstated. It also sits badly with the principle, which says blood clots 'slowly or not at all'.
entries.change: Now 'K, blood that clots slowly' and 'lack of vitamin K slows clotting'.

entries.finding: The stomach releases pepsinogen, not pepsin, and the pancreas releases trypsinogen
entries.reason: Over-reach. 'Gastric juice contains pepsin' and 'trypsin from the pancreas' are what the syllabus says. How the enzymes are activated is beyond it.

entries.finding: Exam tip implies pancreatic lipase is the first enzyme to act on fat
entries.reason: A syllabus simplification stated as fact (check 11), since lingual and gastric lipase act earlier. Fixed by scoping it to the syllabus, not by teaching those enzymes.
entries.change: Exam tip now says 'remember where the syllabus places the first enzyme for each food'.

entries.finding: Hint 3 'Bile from III and IV contains no enzymes at all' leaks into Q24
entries.reason: This tells a student still on Q23 which labels handle bile, the key step in Q24. It also says IV supplies bile, which pushes them towards the D trap.
entries.change: Hint 3 now reads 'Neither III nor IV makes acid or pepsin. Between I and II, which one does the oesophagus open straight into?'

entries.finding: Solution says none of the stomach's secretions digests fat
entries.reason: Misread. The A line says that none of pepsin, rennin and hydrochloric acid digests fat, scoped with 'in the syllabus'. That is true. The solution never mentions all of the stomach's secretions.

entries.finding: Lipase acts on the fat inside the droplets, not on the droplets themselves
entries.reason: The wording mixed up bile's job (making droplets) with lipase's job (splitting fat).
entries.change: Hint 2 and the principle now say lipase splits the fat in those droplets into fatty acids and glycerol.

entries.finding: Diagram has no alt text
entries.reason: Alt text is written separately in out/diagrams/biology-waec.alt.json and is not part of the teaching item.

entries.finding: 'the gall bladder only stores it', 'does not make or secrete bile' and 'Fat is digested in two steps in the small intestine'
entries.reason: The gall bladder also concentrates and releases bile, and some fat is digested before the small intestine. The key depends on the examiner's reading that storing is not secreting, so that reading is now stated as a convention.
entries.change: D line now says the gall bladder stores and releases bile but does not make it, so it is not counted as secreting bile. Exam tip now says 'stores it but does not make it'. Principle now says 'digested mainly in the small intestine'.

entries.finding: Hint 3 names 'the stomach labelled I', which answers Q23
entries.reason: Check 12 does not say which direction a leak goes, and the question navigator lets a student read Q24's hints before answering Q23. Q24 loses nothing by the change.
entries.change: Hint 3 now says 'two labels that are easy to include by mistake, I and IV' and leaves the student to identify them.

entries.finding: Villi line the whole small intestine, not just the ileum
entries.reason: Writing 'small intestine (ileum)' treated the two as one and the same.
entries.change: Principle now says 'on the inner wall of the small intestine, especially the ileum', and 'projections' replaces 'folds'.

entries.finding: Most water is absorbed in the small intestine, not the colon
entries.reason: This is already scoped. Hint 2 and the B line both say that in the syllabus the colon takes up water, and a correctly scoped syllabus claim passes check 11.

entries.finding: 'Only the uptake of nutrients suffers' is too absolute
entries.reason: A syllabus simplification ('villi are for absorption') stated as fact (check 11). The key itself says 'only', so the fix scopes the claim and does not argue against the key.
entries.change: How to tell now says 'In the syllabus, villi are for absorption, so the problem is taken to be with absorbing nutrients only.' D line now says the syllabus treats only absorption as affected, and that bile helps digestion but does not digest food itself.

entries.finding: Hint 2 says temperature and light 'affect every habitat'
entries.reason: Light does not reach caves or deep water.
entries.change: Now 'affect land and water habitats alike'.

entries.finding: A hygrometer does not usually have two thermometers
entries.reason: Only the wet-and-dry-bulb type has two, so 'usually' was not scoped (check 11).
entries.change: D line now says 'the kind used in school has two thermometers, one with a wet bulb'.

entries.finding: Hints give away Q30 (measures a factor in water): hint 1 'where it is being put', hint 2 'pushed down into water', hint 3 'measure conditions in the air, not in water'
entries.reason: This is the case the standard names. A student still working on Q29 is told the Q30 answer.
entries.change: All three hints rewritten so none mentions water, air or where the instrument sits. Hint 1 points to its shape and painted pattern. Hint 2 rules out the wind vane and hygrometer by how they look. Hint 3 asks which remaining option is a U-shaped glass tube and whether the drawing shows one.

entries.finding: A Secchi disc measures transparency, not turbidity
entries.reason: Over-reach. The syllabus pairs the Secchi disc with turbidity, and the solution explains that as how clear or cloudy the water is.

entries.finding: Exam tip makes absolute claims about anything lowered, pushed in or mounted
entries.reason: Unscoped absolutes (checks 5 and 11).
entries.change: Exam tip now says the way an instrument is used 'usually' tells you its habitat, and gives one named instrument for each habitat.

entries.finding: Q30 hints say 'the disc', and Q29's answer is Secchi disc
entries.reason: The word names only the shape a sighted student can see in the drawing. Hint 1 asks the student to name the instrument from Q29 but does not name it.

entries.finding: Says a real population wobbles, then says it stays the same
entries.reason: Self-contradiction (check 11). The standard gives this exact case.
entries.change: Principle now says the population 'is taken as constant' and that a real pond's ups and downs stay close to that level. Exam tip now says 'is taken as constant'.

entries.finding: Difficulty should be easy
entries.reason: Difficulty is a judgment call and this one is not clearly wrong. The A distractor is subtle, and the standard counts a subtle distractor as hard.

entries.finding: Producers do not eat the level below
entries.reason: Fact error in hint 3 and the D line.
entries.change: Hint 3 and the D line now say producers get energy from sunlight and each consumer level feeds on the level below.

entries.finding: Exam tip: 'the order is always nutrients, algal bloom ... death of aquatic life'
entries.reason: Enrichment does not always go as far as killing aquatic life. This is the syllabus sequence.
entries.change: Now 'the order the syllabus expects is'.

entries.finding: Treats frequency as the number of plants counted
entries.reason: Frequency is how often a species turns up across quadrats. The question misuses the word, so the teaching answers as keyed and still gives the correct meaning.
entries.change: Hint 2 and the principle now say the question calls 1,850 a frequency, give the real meaning of frequency, and use 1,850 as the plant count for this calculation.

entries.finding: The plant unit is dropped from the working
entries.reason: The standard asks for units to be carried through.
entries.change: Working line now reads '= 1,850 plants ÷ 100 m²'.

entries.finding: Splitting 'acts on the germ' from 'acts on the host' does not hold up, and the exam tip puts vaccination with diet and rest
entries.reason: Vaccination is a way of controlling disease. A student following the old tip would pick vaccination as the option that does not control pathogens.
entries.change: Exam tip now sets methods against the pathogen or its carrier apart from general health habits, and says vaccination counts as a control method. The principle and How to tell now call the balanced diet a general health habit that does not kill the pathogen, stop it breeding or stop it spreading.

entries.finding: Saying UV lamps sterilise water and equipment is too absolute
entries.reason: Over-reach at syllabus level. 'UV sterilises' is how schools describe it.

entries.finding: A line says deforestation never creates habitats
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute (check 11). Cleared land becomes a different, disturbed habitat.
entries.change: A line now says deforestation mainly destroys habitats, and cleared land may suit a few other species, but that is not its main effect.

entries.finding: 'nothing holds the topsoil in place'
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute. Grass and weeds still hold some soil.
entries.change: Now 'little is left to hold the topsoil in place'.

entries.finding: 'Only a natural resource can be conserved' is false outside the syllabus
entries.reason: The standard gives this exact case. Energy and buildings are conserved too.
entries.change: The principle and hint 2 now open with 'In Biology, conservation means'. The 'Only a natural resource' sentence is gone.

entries.finding: Treats all felling as against conservation
entries.reason: Controlled, selective felling is itself one of the syllabus conservation methods (check 11).
entries.change: Principle now says felling as the option puts it, with no control and no replanting, works against conservation, and that controlled felling followed by replanting can be part of it. Exam tip now says the other options 'usually' add to or protect the resource.

entries.finding: Tree-crop plantations can harm natural forests
entries.reason: Over-reach. The syllabus counts planting tree crops as conservation, and the D line makes no absolute claim.

entries.finding: Defines an adaptation as a feature the whole species shares
entries.reason: Adaptive traits can vary within a species, so this was a false universal (checks 8 and 11).
entries.change: The principle and exam tip now define an adaptation as a feature that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its habitat. Hint 2, How to tell, and the C and D lines now rest on 'a difference between individuals with no link to survival in a habitat'.

entries.finding: 'tasters and non-tasters look exactly the same'
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute.
entries.change: A line now says a taster's tongue looks the same as a non-taster's.

entries.finding: 'no taste at all' to non-tasters is too absolute
entries.reason: To non-tasters it is tasteless or only slightly bitter.
entries.change: Now 'has little or no taste to others'.

entries.finding: The size sequence shows an allele as a smaller part inside a gene
entries.reason: Conceptual error. An allele is a version of a gene.
entries.change: The sequence now stops at gene and is followed by 'An allele is one version of that gene, not a smaller part of it'.

entries.finding: 'The two alleles of a gene' needs the context of a body cell with paired chromosomes
entries.reason: A one-phrase fix that stops a student thinking every gene has exactly two alleles.
entries.change: Now 'In a body cell, the two alleles a person carries for a gene sit at the same position'.

entries.finding: Exam tip calls the nucleus a true answer although the stem says 'found on'
entries.reason: The tip says alleles are inside the nucleus, which is true, and it teaches picking the most exact option. It never says they are 'on' the nucleus.

entries.finding: 'A gene is a short length of DNA that controls one characteristic'
entries.reason: Many characteristics depend on several genes, and one gene can affect more than one. 'One' is an absolute the syllabus does not need.
entries.change: Now 'controls a characteristic'.

entries.finding: 'always gives' 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa
entries.reason: That is the expected ratio, not a guaranteed count among one couple's children.
entries.change: Exam tip now says 'gives an expected ratio of' and 'For each child, the chance of the recessive trait showing is ¼'.

entries.finding: Hint 3 paraphrases option C
entries.reason: A student could match the wording without remembering the theory (check 2).
entries.change: Hint 3 now asks the student to recall the second part of Lamarck's theory: what happens to a change an animal gains through use or disuse.

entries.finding: The queen lays all the eggs and the workers are sterile
entries.reason: A syllabus simplification stated as absolute (check 11). Workers can lay eggs in a hive with no queen.
entries.change: Principle now says the queen is the main fertile female and lays nearly all the eggs, and workers do not normally breed. Hint 2 now says 'main egg-laying female' and 'males on a flight outside the hive'.

entries.finding: A drone's only job is to mate
entries.reason: Unscoped absolute.
entries.change: Now 'whose main job is to mate with a queen'.

entries.finding: Leaves out that the variation must be inherited
entries.reason: Without it, 'pass their useful features on' reads like Lamarck.
entries.change: Principle now says those with inherited features that suit their surroundings are more likely to survive, reproduce and pass those features on. 'survive' became 'are more likely to survive'.

entries.finding: Darwin and Wallace reached the idea separately, not together
entries.reason: Fact error.
entries.change: Now 'Alfred Russel Wallace reached the same idea on his own'.
